evidence: createApp registers Express routes (app.post/app.get/app.patch) — transport responsibility appropriate to infrastructure
Route handlers delegate to service.addProduct/placeOrder/listOrders/progressOrder/cancelOrder; no stock or transition rules are computed in this file
isRecord and the fulfilmentStates checks on req.body/req.query only validate request shape before calling the application layer
Error middleware maps DomainError codes (ORDER_NOT_FOUND, PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND, INSUFFICIENT_STOCK) to HTTP 404/409/400 — a transport concern
Default parameter new OrderService(new InMemoryProductRepository(), new InMemoryOrderRepository()) is composition wiring, acceptable in infrastructure
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-server.ts does the work an infrastructure/transport adapter should do. It registers Express routes, parses and shape-checks request bodies and query parameters, maps domain objects to JSON views, and turns DomainError codes into HTTP status codes. It also wires up default dependencies in the createApp default parameter, which is composition work and fits infrastructure. The business operations themselves are delegated to OrderService: addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, progressOrder and cancelOrder. Stock rules, state-transition rules and order invariants are not re-implemented here. The state checks against fulfilmentStates are input parsing, done so the request can be converted into typed arguments, and they reuse the domain's own constant instead of redefining business rules. One minor point: the file throws DomainError for request-format errors and lists the 'cancelled' literal next to fulfilmentStates. That is a small style issue, not a misplaced responsibility.
